---
title: "Overview"
---

## What is Sprout?

Sprout is a Python package that is designed to help build a [data
package](https://data-pkg-guide.seedcase-project.org). Importantly, Sprout
provides tools to create high-quality metadata that is accurately connected to
the data. Specifically, Sprout builds prepared and tidied data and
well-documented metadata into the core components of a data package:

- **Data** in a [tidy
  format](https://sprout.seedcase-project.org/docs/design/interface/inputs),
  stored in [Apache
  Parquet](https://decisions.seedcase-project.org/why-parquet/) format in a
  standardized location.
- **Metadata** that follows specific standards (currently the [Frictionless Data
  Package
  specification](https://decisions.seedcase-project.org/why-frictionless-data/))
  that correctly connects to the underlying data.

Once these are built in the data package, they are ready for bundling,
versioning, and distribution to be shared and used.

## Why use it?

There are many tools for processing, cleaning, and transforming data, and for
storing them in databases on servers and building data warehouses. However, few
tools are specifically designed around building a set of data that follows basic
software development lifecycle practices and principles. In particular, as a
cohesive and reproducible package development processes that can be easily
audited, versioned, and distributed.

Sprout integrates a few key standards and practices to help build a fantastic
dataset *along with its metadata*. In that way, it ensures the data will be more
easily usable for later analysis, for finding the right data needed for the
analysis, and for better understanding of what is actually in the data.

Sprout has two main component: a command-line interface (CLI) and a Python
library. The CLI is used to simplify the process of creating metadata and
building up the pieces of the data package, while the Python library contains
tools to help with programmatic extraction and creation of metadata.

## Learning more

This website contains documentation on Sprout's design, how to use it, and
details about the interface.

- [How-to guide](/docs/guide/index.qmd): The guide section provides a
  step-by-step introduction to using Sprout, including installation, setup, and
  creating and managing data packages.
- [Reference](/docs/reference/index.qmd): The reference section contains
  detailed information about the Sprout Python Package API, specifically the
  documentation of individual classes, methods, and functions.
- [Design](/docs/design/index.qmd): The design section describes the
  architecture and interface of Sprout, the requirements, use-cases, user
  personas, and the [C4 model](https://c4model.com/).

If you are interested in learning more about similar tools, we have only found a
few that are related though with quite different purposes and use-cases, such
as:

- [Open Data Editor](https://opendataeditor.okfn.org/): Is a web- and
  click-based tool for creating and editing data packages.
- [gen3](https://gen3.org/): Is a web-based platform for building data commons.
